katas.title: Snapshot fields: escape the delimiter first, then backslashes

defects.scenario: A product or customer name containing `|` (e.g. "Pens | Blue") is saved and the snapshot is loaded on the next start.
defects.consequence: The backslash that escapes the pipe is itself doubled by the second replace, so the field is written as `Pens \\| Blue`; split() reads `\\` as one literal backslash and the bare `|` as a field separator. The row gains a field, `count(...)` rejects it, and the whole snapshot fails to load ("Unexpected field count."): one name locks the shop out of its own data.

katas.title: Order.getItems: return an unmodifiable view instead of copying every line
katas.findingRef: j7 aggregate ownership of order lines (astraupskill/02-CONCEPTS.md:3)

provenance.find: An aggregate is a group of related values with rules that must stay consistent through an operation.

defects.scenario: Any caller (the CLI listing, the snapshot writer, a future HTTP handler) reads a PAID order and calls `setQuantity` on a returned line.
defects.consequence: The list cannot be resized, but its elements are the order's OWN mutable OrderItem objects: `getItems().get(0).setQuantity(99)` changes a paid order's quantity and subtotal with no ensureEditable and no discount check, so the aggregate's invariants (paid orders are frozen, discount <= subtotal) can be broken from outside.

defects.scenario: The mutator the view hands out.
defects.consequence: OrderItem is mutable (public setQuantity), so only copies may leave the aggregate; that is what the original stream().map(OrderItem::copy) did.

katas.title: Order.setItemQuantity: update the existing line in place instead of building a candidate

provenance.find: The intended update path is `service.updateItemQuantity(orderId, productId, quantity)`.

defects.scenario: An order has 2 x 10.00 with a 15.00 discount; the clerk lowers the quantity to 1.
defects.consequence: The line is changed BEFORE the discount check. The check still throws "Reduce the discount before reducing the subtotal.", so the clerk sees a refusal, but the quantity is already 1: the order now has subtotal 10.00, discount 15.00 and a total of -5.00, and the next save writes it. A rejected command must leave the aggregate unchanged.
